passages: This man is literally strapping a camera to a pigeon. And then he just lets it fly away!
Julius Neubronner was a pharmacist in a little German town, and his pigeons already delivered his medicine. So he built a camera small enough for a bird to wear.
You see, a tiny rubber ball was pumped full of air before take-off. As it slowly leaked, it worked like a timer, and when it went flat, click! The shutter fired, high above the rooftops.
The patent office said it was impossible. So he sent them the photos, and got his patent.
At a big exhibition in Dresden, crowds watched the pigeons land, and their aerial photos were turned into postcards on the spot. Some of them even show the pigeon's own wingtips!
